before: Know your area's flood risk and the nearest high ground / relief camp
Prepare an emergency kit: water (3 L/person/day), dry food, torch, radio, power bank, first-aid
Keep documents (ID, insurance, land papers, medical records) in a waterproof pouch
Save emergency numbers on your phone and on paper
Agree a family meeting point and plan an evacuation route
Move valuables, electronics and chemicals to upper floors
Keep a month's supply of regular medicines
Fill vehicle fuel tank and charge all phones and power banks
Install the IMD / state alert apps (e.g. Mausam, Umang) and follow warnings
Know how to switch off the main electricity and gas supply
during: Move to higher ground immediately when told to evacuate - do not wait
Switch off electricity at the main switch and shut gas cylinders
Never walk, swim or drive through flood water (15 cm can knock you down)
Stay away from power lines, drains and open manholes
Drink only boiled or chlorinated water; avoid flood-water contact
Keep listening to radio / official alerts for updates
Help children, elderly, pregnant women and disabled people first
If trapped, climb to the roof, signal with a bright cloth or torch and call 112 / 1077
Carry your emergency kit and documents when leaving
after: Return home only when authorities declare it safe
Check for structural damage, cracks and gas leaks before entering
Do not switch on electricity until an electrician has checked the wiring
Photograph damage for insurance and relief claims
Throw away food that touched flood water; boil all drinking water
Clean and disinfect walls and floors; watch for snakes and insects
Get vaccinated / treated for cuts, diarrhoea or fever (leptospirosis, cholera, dengue risk)
Register for government relief at the local Tehsil / Panchayat office
Check on neighbours, especially elderly people living alone

before: Track IMD cyclone warnings (Yellow / Orange / Red) and heed evacuation advisories
Identify your nearest cyclone shelter and a safe route to it
Secure the roof, doors and windows; trim loose branches near the house
Store 7 days of dry food and drinking water
Keep radio, torch, spare batteries and power bank ready
Keep documents and cash in a waterproof bag
Fishermen: bring boats and nets to safe harbour and do not venture to sea
Secure or bring in loose objects, hoardings and cattle
Charge phones and fill fuel tank
during: Stay indoors, away from windows and glass, in the strongest room
Turn off electricity and gas; avoid using electrical appliances
If your house is unsafe, go to the designated cyclone shelter before winds rise
Do not go out during the calm 'eye' of the storm - winds return suddenly
Keep listening to battery radio for official instructions
Stay away from beaches, rivers and low coastal areas (storm surge)
Use a mattress or blankets to protect yourself if roof starts to fail
Call 112 or 1077 for life-threatening emergencies only
after: Stay in shelter until officials say the cyclone has fully passed
Avoid fallen power lines, broken poles and damaged buildings
Beware of flooded roads and uprooted trees
Drink only safe water; boil it if unsure
Document damage with photos for relief and insurance
Provide first aid to injured people and call 108 when needed
Do not enter the sea until the warning is withdrawn (fishermen)
Help with community clean-up and check on neighbours

flood.title: 1. Get the warning and stay informed
steps: Monitor Central Water Commission and IMD alerts, local radio and your SDMA's messages.
Understand terms: 'Watch' = flooding possible, 'Warning' = flooding happening or imminent.
Do not rely on rumours; confirm through official channels.

flood.title: 2. Prepare your home and family
steps: Raise valuables and electrical items above expected water level.
Block drains and toilets with sandbags / sealed plastic to prevent backflow.
Pack the emergency kit and brief everyone on the evacuation plan.

flood.title: 3. Evacuate early
steps: Leave as soon as authorities advise. Roads can flood within minutes.
Switch off power and gas, lock the house and take your kit.
Use designated routes; never take shortcuts through water.
Go to the nearest relief camp or higher ground and register with the camp in-charge.

flood.title: 4. If you are trapped
steps: Move to the highest safe point (upper floor / roof). Do not go into a closed attic.
Call 112, 1077 or NDRF 9711077372 - share your location and number of people.
Signal with a torch, whistle or bright cloth.
Stay together and conserve phone battery.

flood.title: 5. Driving & walking safety
steps: Turn around, don't drown - 30 cm of water can float a car.
If your vehicle stalls in rising water, abandon it and move to high ground.
Avoid walking through moving water and stay away from bridges over fast water.

flood.title: 6. Health & water safety
steps: Boil water for at least 1 minute or use chlorine tablets.
Wash hands with soap; avoid flood water contact with wounds.
Seek medical help for fever, diarrhoea, or skin infections.

flood.title: 7. Recovery
steps: Return only when declared safe; inspect for structural damage.
Get wiring checked before restoring power.
Document losses and apply for relief / insurance.

cyclone.title: 1. Understand the warning stages
steps: IMD issues Pre-cyclone Watch (72 h), Cyclone Alert (48 h), Warning (24 h) and Post-landfall Outlook.
Colour codes: Green (no action), Yellow (be aware), Orange (be prepared), Red (take action).
Follow your district administration's evacuation advisories.

cyclone.title: 2. Secure your home
steps: Strengthen the roof with ropes / weights; close and bolt doors and windows.
Remove loose objects from the courtyard and roof.
Cut weak branches; park vehicles in a safe, sheltered spot.

cyclone.title: 3. Build your kit
steps: Water, dry food, medicines, first-aid, torch, radio, batteries, power bank.
Waterproof pouch with documents, cash and a list of contacts.
Blankets, clothes, hygiene supplies and baby / elderly care items.

cyclone.title: 4. Evacuate to a cyclone shelter
steps: Move to a pucca building / cyclone shelter in low-lying coastal zones.
Go before the winds pick up; roads may become impassable.
Carry the kit, keep family together, register at the shelter.

cyclone.title: 5. During the storm
steps: Stay inside in the strongest, innermost room away from windows.
Do not step outside during the eye of the cyclone.
Keep a battery radio on for updates; avoid candles - use torches.

cyclone.title: 6. At sea / coast
steps: Fishermen must return to harbour on first warning.
Move boats and nets to safe places; do not stay near the shore.
Beware of storm surge - sea water can rush several kilometres inland.

cyclone.title: 7. After the cyclone
steps: Wait for the 'all clear' from authorities.
Avoid fallen wires and weakened structures.
Give first aid, call 108 for serious injuries, and share news of missing people with 112.
